messages:
From: Lina Gomez <ops@sapphire.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: support@sapphire.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden throughput drop + intermittent WS timeouts (production)

Hi David,

We're seeing a serious regression in our live ingestion pipeline connected to Redwood. Starting ~08:45 PST this morning, our per-connection throughput dropped from a steady ~1200 reqs/min to <150 reqs/min. In addition, our clients are intermittently seeing WebSocket stalls and chunked transfer timeouts (WS close code 1006 / 504-level timeouts from our gateway). This is impacting several downstream features and one critical customer demo.

Symptoms:
- Error spikes: 5xx responses from /v1/realtime/generate and sporadic 1006 closes
- Latency: 95th percentile token latency jumped from ~180ms to ~1.8s
- Throughput: aggregate token/sec down ~85% for a subset of hosts (us-west-2)
- We captured a sample trace and logs (attached: sapphire_error_log_1106.txt, sample_trace_1106.pcap)

We've opened a PagerDuty incident (PD-4782) and placed a temporary routing rule to failover to a secondary model, but it only partially mitigates the issue. Can you triage immediately and loop in engineering?

Thanks,
Lina Gomez--

Subject: RE: Sudden throughput drop + intermittent WS timeouts (production) — triage notes

Team — quick triage log: 

- Observed matching error patterns in our ingress edge logs: repeated 502/504 from the proxy layer between 08:44–09:05 PST in us-west-2.
- Proxy metrics show connection queue build-up and an increase in downstream socket resets.
- Kernel-level dmesg entries correlate to high ephemeral port exhaustion on two hosts (host-rt-02, host-rt-05) — investigating file descriptor leaks.
- Realtime host telemetry: CPU and GPU utilization normal, but backlog on the write path and continuous small stalls in the chunked transfer stream.

Immediate remediation actions taken:
1) Scaled a dedicated pool by spinning additional hosts in us-west-2 and draining host-rt-02/05 for inspection.
2) Increased proxy keepalive and lowered max outstanding requests per connection to reduce buffering.
3) Deployed a temporary gateway rule to route 30% of traffic to eu-west fallback while we monitor for regressions.

Ask from CS/accounting: if this is not stabilized in 60 minutes, we need to prepare an exec briefing and proposed compensation/credits. Monica — can you prep the customer-facing summary and possible credit options?

I'll follow with logs and the candidate root cause in the next update.

—Karthik
